UNDP/ILO or UNDP India 2017-2018 transgender workplace study: could not locate the document; only secondary mentions (thesis, news) seen. Nothing included beyond the 2010 UNDP issue brief.
Pew 2019 India level of acceptance of homosexuality (37% reported by NPR/Equaldex): Pew page opened only states a 22-point rise since 2014; the 37% value was not visible in the text, so not included.
Pew 2013 India figure and ILGA polls on India attitudes: not opened/not found.
Ipsos 2023-2025 India-specific LGBT+ figures: not found; only the 2021 urban India release was opened.

BCG/IIM Ahmedabad/Pride Circle campus survey (64% of 1,700+ students discriminated/ridiculed; 92% mocking, 59% bullying, 26% exclusion): seen only in a Careers360 news article; the report itself was not opened.

BCG 2023 trans workplace survey (90% negative experiences) and Deloitte LGBT+ Inclusion @ Work, Careernet Prism (60% harassment, 73% skip reporting): primary documents not opened (BCG page returned 403).

Bridge (Kolkata) survey of 900+ LGBTQ+ people in 7 eastern/north-eastern states (Dec 2025) and HimKai Arunachal survey (61 responses): only news summaries seen, no school-bullying percentages verified.

NHRC West Bengal 2021 study ('nearly half left households'), 2015 Kerala survey (58% dropped out before Class 10), ICJ 'Living with Dignity' 2019 and ICJ 'Unnatural Offences' 2017: seen only as citations in secondary articles; ICJ reports are narrative with no sample percentages verified.

Humsafar Trust other surveys, Sangama, Naz Foundation (India) Trust, Lawyers Collective, Mitr Trust, Sappho for Equality, Prakriti, TISS: no survey with verifiable percentages found. Only the Humsafar 2010 MSM mental-health baseline (n=150) and Humsafar crisis cases quoted in Li 2017 were verified; the Mitr Clinic (Hyderabad) paper is peer-reviewed and included.
PUCL-K 2001 (Bangalore sexuality minorities) and 2003/Ondede 2014 transgender reports: opened; narrative fact-finding with testimonies, no percentages, so none included.

Corrective rape and forced marriage prevalence: no quantitative Indian survey found; a student paper cites 15 documented cases of corrective rape (secondary, not included). Only a qualitative mention (Ujagare 2026) is included.

Share who never reported violence to police and reasons: no Indian survey with this figure found. Only proxies included (31.3% of 16 Humsafar cases sought legal recourse; 18% of bullied youth reported to school authorities).

Sex-reassignment surgery cost: no verified survey figure. NHRC report text gives Rs 3-5 lakh for one surgery type but the wording is unclear and was not included; press ranges (Rs 2-8 lakh) not verified.
Press-reported 'suicide attempt rate about 31% / half attempted before age 20' for Indian transgender people: appears only as an uncited statement in a 2019 paper; not included.
Virupaksha 2016 review (suicide attempt rate 32-50% across countries) is international, not India-specific; not included.
Khuman 2024 Frontiers in Sociology newspaper content analysis (2005-2022): qualitative, no figures extracted. Kar 2023 (135 reports, 2011-2021) is a separate sample from the 164-report 2025 review.
Lancet, Lancet Psychiatry and Lancet Regional Health SE Asia items found (2024-2025) were commentaries without survey data; NIMHANS-authored LGBT survey with numbers not found.
Indian Journal of Psychiatry: no original prevalence study of LGBT suicidality found; included IJP 2023 narrative review (one Indian coming-out study) only.
